name: Amygdala
summary: An almond-shaped group of nuclei in the anteromedial temporal lobe, in front of the hippocampal head and beneath the uncus, at the tip of the temporal horn. It attaches emotional significance to sensory input: the lateral and basolateral nuclei receive highly processed sensory and prefrontal input, the central nucleus sends output to the hypothalamus and brainstem for autonomic and behavioral fear responses, and the corticomedial group receives olfactory input. It drives fear conditioning, threat detection and emotional memory, and its bilateral loss produces the placidity, hyperorality and hypersexuality of the Klüver–Bucy syndrome.

anatomy.location: Anteromedial temporal lobe at the anterior end of the temporal horn, in front of and partly above the hippocampal head, below the lentiform nucleus (with which it is continuous through the substantia innominata) and medial to the temporal pole white matter; its output pathways are the stria terminalis and the ventral amygdalofugal pathway.

subdivisions.name: Basolateral group (lateral, basal, accessory basal nuclei)
subdivisions.note: sensory and prefrontal input; emotional learning

subdivisions.name: Central nucleus
subdivisions.note: output to hypothalamus, periaqueductal gray, brainstem autonomic nuclei: fear expression

subdivisions.name: Bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (extended amygdala)

efferents.via: stria terminalis and ventral amygdalofugal pathway

function: Fear and threat processing, emotional conditioning, assignment of emotional value to stimuli and memories, autonomic and endocrine responses to emotion, social recognition of facial expression, olfactory-emotional integration.

imaging.normalAppearance: Homogeneous gray matter at the anterior tip of the temporal horn on coronal T1, above and in front of the hippocampal head and beneath the uncus; the MASSP mesh in this atlas outlines it. Involved together with the hippocampus in encephalitis and sclerosis.

pathology.finding: FLAIR hyperintensity and swelling of the amygdala and hippocampus.

pathology.pathology: Amygdala enlargement in temporal lobe epilepsy
pathology.finding: Enlarged, mildly T2-bright amygdala on the side of seizure onset.
Bilateral symmetrical amygdala calcification with absent fear responses.

examination: Ask about ictal fear, palpitations or gastric sensations
pearls: A temporal lobe seizure that begins with intense fear and a rising epigastric sensation points to the amygdala and hippocampus
The Klüver–Bucy syndrome after herpes encephalitis or bilateral temporal surgery is the human evidence for amygdala function
